issue: Does fugitive tolling apply to suspend the running of a supervised release term when the releasee absconds?

sides.position: Fugitive tolling applies in the supervised release context, so the term is suspended while the releasee is a fugitive.
cases: United States v. Barinas, 865 F.3d 99 (2d Cir. 2017)
United States v. Island, 916 F.3d 249 (3d Cir. 2019)
United States v. Buchanan, 638 F.3d 448 (4th Cir. 2011)
United States v. Murguia-Oliveros, 421 F.3d 951 (9th Cir. 2005)

sides.position: Fugitive tolling does not apply in the supervised release context.
cases: United States v. Hernandez-Ferrer, 599 F.3d 63 (1st Cir. 2010)
United States v. Talley, 83 F.4th 1296 (11th Cir. 2023)

quote: We begin by explaining there is currently a four-to-two circuit split on whether fugitive tolling exists in the supervised release context: the Second, Third, Fourth, and Ninth Circuits hold that it does; the First and Eleventh Circuits hold that it does not.
cite: United States v. Swick, 137 F.4th 336 (5th Cir. 2025)
